rooms.title: La cocina de la abuela
rooms.subtitle: Grandma's kitchen
rooms.focus: Regular verbs: one clue per sentence

puzzles.sentence_pre: Todas las mañanas, en la radio
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Todas las mañanas" (every morning) marks a habit. Habits and repeated actions in the past take the imperfect: sonaban.
puzzles.translation: Every morning, old boleros used to play on the radio.

puzzles.sentence_pre: El viejo reloj de la pared siempre
puzzles.rule_feedback: This describes how the clock usually was, not one event. Descriptions and habits ("siempre") take the imperfect: marcaba.
puzzles.translation: The old wall clock was always five minutes slow.

puzzles.sentence_post: la cocina con una luz cálida.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Por las noches" (at night, every night) sets a repeated background scene. Use the imperfect: iluminaba.
puzzles.translation: At night, the lamp lit the kitchen with a warm light.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Mientras la abuela cocinaba, la tetera
puzzles.rule_feedback: "De repente" (suddenly) marks a single action that interrupts the background ("cocinaba"). Sudden, completed actions take the preterite: empezó.
puzzles.translation: While grandma was cooking, the kettle suddenly started to whistle.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Entonces el gato saltó a la mesa y
puzzles.rule_feedback: This is a chain of completed events: first "saltó", then the next action. Events that move the story forward take the preterite: tiró.
puzzles.translation: Then the cat jumped onto the table and knocked a plate onto the floor.

rooms.title: El salón en invierno
rooms.subtitle: The living room in winter
rooms.focus: Common irregulars: hacer, poner, tener, venir, ser

puzzles.rule_feedback: Weather that sets the scene is background description, so it takes the imperfect: hacía. The preterite of hacer is irregular (hice, hizo), but it doesn't fit here.
puzzles.translation: It was winter and it was very cold outside.

puzzles.rule_feedback: Describing how people looked or what they were like takes the imperfect. Ser is irregular in the imperfect: era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran.
puzzles.translation: In that photo, my grandparents were very young.

puzzles.rule_feedback: "Cada tarde" (every afternoon) is a routine, so use the imperfect: tenía. Tuvo (irregular stem tuv-) is for a single completed event.
puzzles.translation: Every afternoon, my sister had to practise the piano.

puzzles.rule_feedback: "De repente" signals one sudden, completed action, so use the preterite. Poner has an irregular stem, pus-: puse, pusiste, puso.
puzzles.translation: Suddenly, Dad put more wood in the fireplace.

puzzles.sentence_post: el tío Pepe con un regalo enorme.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Entonces" (then) moves the story forward with a new event, so use the preterite. Venir has an irregular stem, vin-: vine, viniste, vino.
puzzles.translation: Then Uncle Pepe came with an enormous present.

rooms.title: El dormitorio de la infancia
rooms.subtitle: The childhood bedroom
rooms.focus: Both tenses in one sentence, heavy irregulars: ser, ir, estar, caer

puzzles.sentence_post: pequeño, soñaba con viajar por todo el mundo.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Cuando era pequeño" (when I was little) describes a stage of life, which is background. Use the imperfect: era. Careful: fui is the preterite of both ser and ir.
puzzles.translation: When I was little, I dreamed of travelling all over the world.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Cuando llegué a casa, el cielo
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Llegué" is the event; the sky is the scene it happened in. States and descriptions take the imperfect: estaba. Estuvo (stem estuv-) would mean a closed period.
puzzles.translation: When I got home, the sky was very cloudy.

puzzles.sentence_post: a la cama cuando, de repente, sonó el teléfono.
puzzles.rule_feedback: An action already in progress that gets interrupted ("sonó") takes the imperfect. Ir is one of only three irregular imperfects: iba, ibas, iba (the others are ser and ver).
puzzles.translation: I was already going to bed when, suddenly, the phone rang.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Mientras yo dormía, un libro se
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Dormía" is the background; the book falling is the single event that interrupts it. Use the preterite. Caer changes i to y: cayó, cayeron.
puzzles.translation: While I was sleeping, a book fell off the shelf.

puzzles.sentence_post: al mercado y compré flores frescas.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Esa mañana" (that morning) points to one specific occasion, followed by another completed action ("compré"). Use the preterite: fui. It is the same form as ser's preterite, so context tells you which verb it is.
puzzles.translation: That morning I went to the market and bought fresh flowers.

rooms.title: La cafetería de la esquina
rooms.subtitle: The corner café
rooms.focus: Stem-changing verbs: servir, dormir, pedir, sentir

puzzles.rule_feedback: "Cada mañana" marks a routine, so use the imperfect: servía. Good news: stem-changing verbs are regular in the imperfect. The e→i change only appears in the preterite (sirvió).
puzzles.translation: Every morning, the waiter served coffee to the same customers.

puzzles.sentence_post: y la gente corría con paraguas.
puzzles.rule_feedback: Weather as the background of a scene takes the imperfect: llovía. "Corría" is background too; nothing has happened yet.
puzzles.translation: Outside it was raining and people were running with umbrellas.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Mientras hablábamos, el perro del dueño
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Mientras hablábamos" sets up a background, and the sleeping dog is part of it: dormía. Dormir changes o→u only in the preterite (durmió).
puzzles.translation: While we were talking, the owner's dog was sleeping under the table.

puzzles.rule_feedback: "Esa tarde" (that afternoon) is one specific occasion, and ordering is a single completed action: pidió. Pedir changes e→i in the third person preterite: pidió, pidieron.
puzzles.translation: That afternoon, my friend ordered hot chocolate with churros.

puzzles.sentence_post: un olor a pan recién hecho.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "De repente" marks a sudden, one-time perception: sintió. Sentir changes e→i in the third person preterite (sintió, sintieron) but is regular in the imperfect (sentía).
puzzles.translation: Suddenly, my friend noticed the smell of freshly baked bread.

rooms.title: La estación de tren
rooms.subtitle: The train station
rooms.focus: Irregular stems with -j- and -uv-: decir, andar, traer

puzzles.sentence_pre: El reloj de la estación siempre
puzzles.rule_feedback: This describes how the clock usually was, not an event: iba. ("Ir adelantado" means a clock is fast.) Ir is irregular in the imperfect: iba, ibas, iba.
puzzles.translation: The station clock was always five minutes fast.

puzzles.rule_feedback: "Cada cinco minutos" is a repeated action, so use the imperfect: decía. Decir is regular in the imperfect, but its preterite has a -j- stem: dije, dijo, dijeron.
puzzles.translation: Every five minutes, a voice said the same thing over the loudspeaker.

puzzles.sentence_post: de un lado a otro del andén.
puzzles.rule_feedback: Two things going on at the same time in the background ("mientras esperábamos") both take the imperfect: andaba. Andar's preterite is irregular, with a -uv- stem: anduve, anduvo.
puzzles.translation: While we were waiting, a pigeon was walking up and down the platform.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Por fin, a las ocho en punto, el tren
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Por fin" and an exact time ("a las ocho en punto") mark one completed event: llegó.
puzzles.translation: Finally, at exactly eight o'clock, the train arrived at the station.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Mi tía bajó del tren y me
puzzles.rule_feedback: This is a chain of events (bajó, then the next action), so use the preterite: trajo. Traer has a -j- stem in the preterite: traje, trajo, trajeron (not "trajieron").
puzzles.translation: My aunt got off the train and brought me a suitcase full of presents.

rooms.title: El aula de quinto
rooms.subtitle: The fifth-grade classroom
rooms.focus: Verbs that change meaning: saber, conocer, querer, poder

puzzles.sentence_post: todas las capitales de Europa de memoria.
puzzles.rule_feedback: Knowing something over time is a state, so use the imperfect: sabía (I knew). In the preterite, supe means "I found out", which is a different meaning.
puzzles.translation: As a girl, I knew all the capitals of Europe by heart.

puzzles.sentence_post: la verdad: la profesora se jubilaba.
puzzles.rule_feedback: Here saber means "to find out", a moment of discovery. That meaning only exists in the preterite: supe. Sabía would mean "I already knew".
puzzles.translation: That day I found out the truth: the teacher was retiring.

puzzles.sentence_post: a Lucía, la chica nueva de la clase.
puzzles.rule_feedback: Meeting someone for the first time is an event: conocí (I met). Conocía would mean "I already knew her".
puzzles.translation: In September I met Lucía, the new girl in class.

puzzles.sentence_post: salir al recreo antes de tiempo, pero la profesora no nos dejaba.
puzzles.rule_feedback: An ongoing wish is a state: queríamos (we wanted). In the preterite, quisimos suggests we actually tried, and "no quisimos" means "we refused".
puzzles.translation: We always wanted to go out for break early, but the teacher wouldn't let us.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Después de mucho estudiar, por fin
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Por fin" marks a result. In the preterite, poder means "managed to": pude aprobar. Podía only means "I was able to", with no sign that it actually happened.
puzzles.translation: After a lot of studying, I finally managed to pass the maths exam.

rooms.title: El taller del abuelo
rooms.subtitle: Grandpa's workshop
rooms.focus: Irregulars in both tenses: poner, dar, ver, hacer

puzzles.rule_feedback: "Siempre" plus "mientras trabajaba" describes a habit, so use the imperfect: ponía. Poner is regular in the imperfect but irregular in the preterite (puse, puso).
puzzles.translation: While he worked, Grandpa always put the radio on.

puzzles.sentence_post: una luz amarilla sobre la mesa de trabajo.
puzzles.rule_feedback: Describing what a place was like is background, so use the imperfect: daba. Dar's preterite is irregular and has no accent: di, dio.
puzzles.translation: The old lamp gave off a yellow light over the workbench.

puzzles.rule_feedback: What you could see from a place is a description: veíamos. Ver is one of only three irregular imperfects (it keeps the e: veía), along with ser and ir.
puzzles.translation: From the workshop window we could see the sea.

puzzles.sentence_pre: En una sola tarde, el abuelo
puzzles.sentence_post: un barco de madera para mí.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "En una sola tarde" (in a single afternoon) presents the job as finished, so use the preterite: hizo. Watch the spelling: hice, but hizo (c→z).
puzzles.translation: In a single afternoon, Grandpa made me a wooden boat.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Al final del verano, el abuelo me
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Al final del verano" points to one moment when something happened: dio. In the preterite, dar takes -er/-ir endings and no accent: di, diste, dio.
puzzles.translation: At the end of the summer, Grandpa gave me his old toolbox.

rooms.title: La noche de la tormenta
rooms.subtitle: The night of the storm
rooms.focus: Telling a story: setting the scene vs. what happened

puzzles.rule_feedback: "Era de noche" and "hacía viento" set the scene. The rain is part of that scene: llovía.
puzzles.translation: It was night, it was pouring and it was windy.

puzzles.rule_feedback: Describing where someone was and how they felt is background: estaba. Estuvo would present it as a closed, finished period.
puzzles.translation: My grandmother was sitting calmly in her rocking chair.

puzzles.sentence_post: la luz y encendimos una vela.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "De repente" marks the event that breaks into the scene. "Irse la luz" means the power going out: se fue. It's the preterite of ir, which has the same form as ser's.
puzzles.translation: Suddenly, the power went out and we lit a candle.

puzzles.sentence_post: un ruido y la puerta se abrió sola.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "A medianoche" pins the event to one moment, so use the preterite: oímos. In the third person, oír changes i to y: oyó, oyeron.
puzzles.translation: At midnight we heard a noise and the door opened by itself.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Mientras esperábamos a que volviera la luz, el viejo reloj
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Mientras esperábamos" is background, and the clock striking hour after hour is too: daba.
puzzles.translation: While we waited for the power to come back, the old clock struck the hours.

rooms.title: La fiesta de cumpleaños
rooms.subtitle: The birthday party
rooms.focus: Había vs. hubo, plus plural forms: venir, poner

puzzles.rule_feedback: To describe what was in a place, use había (there was / there were). In this meaning, haber stays singular even before plural nouns.
puzzles.translation: In the living room there were balloons of every colour.

puzzles.rule_feedback: Background music during another activity ("mientras comíamos") takes the imperfect: sonaba.
puzzles.translation: While we were eating, seventies music was playing.

puzzles.sentence_post: mis primos con un regalo enorme.
puzzles.rule_feedback: An exact time ("a las seis") marks an arrival, which is an event: vinieron. Venir's preterite stem is vin-: vine, vino, vinieron.
puzzles.translation: At six o'clock my cousins came with an enormous present.

puzzles.sentence_post: la tarta en la mesa y todos cantamos.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Luego" (then) moves the story forward: puso. Poner has an irregular stem, pus-, and no accents: puse, puso.
puzzles.translation: Then my mother put the cake on the table and we all sang.

puzzles.sentence_post: fuegos artificiales y todos salimos al jardín.
puzzles.rule_feedback: Here haber means that something happened (an event), not that something was there. For events, use the preterite: hubo.
puzzles.translation: At midnight there were fireworks and we all went out into the garden.

rooms.title: La despedida
rooms.subtitle: The farewell
rooms.focus: Everything together: closed periods, ir a + infinitive, habits and events

puzzles.sentence_post: en esta casa durante treinta años.
puzzles.rule_feedback: Even a long time counts as one closed block when its length is given and it's over ("durante treinta años"), so use the preterite: vivieron.
puzzles.translation: My parents lived in this house for thirty years.

puzzles.sentence_pre: Todos los domingos, mi madre me
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Todos los domingos" (every Sunday) is a routine: llamaba.
puzzles.translation: Every Sunday, my mother used to call me on the phone.

puzzles.sentence_post: en el jardín y hacía sol.
puzzles.rule_feedback: A photo shows a scene, not an event: estábamos. Note the accent: estábamos.
puzzles.translation: In that photo, we were in the garden and it was sunny.

puzzles.sentence_post: a salir de casa cuando llegó el camión de la mudanza.
puzzles.rule_feedback: "Iba a" + infinitive means "was going to / was about to". It's a plan that gets interrupted ("llegó"), so use the imperfect.
puzzles.translation: I was about to leave the house when the removal van arrived.

puzzles.rule_feedback: "Por última vez" (for the last time) marks a single, final action: cerró.
puzzles.translation: In the end, my father closed the door for the last time.
